question: Mr. I starts from Point M and drives 1 km towards the south. He then takes a right turn, drives 3 km, turns left and drives 3 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 4 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point N. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point M again? (All turns are 90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution:
Given:

Mr. I starts from Point M and drives 1 km towards the south.

He then takes a right turn, drives 3 km, turns left and drives 3 km.

He then takes a left turn and drives 4 km.

He takes a final left turn, drives 4 km and stops at Point N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/724571871777238c4e62c070f04e42d524764cb43c21f31131d7d77d2b377a74.png] 

Thus, Mr. I should drive 1 km (4 km - 3 km) in the west direction in order to reach Point M again.​

Hence, "Option 3" is the correct answer.
